RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel alone is not evidence of sex discrimination. Alleging bias based solely on the interviewers' gender is speculative and will damage your professional standing and credibility.

Once candidates reach the final interview stage, hiring decisions typically hinge on interview performance, references, leadership vision, and institutional fit, rather than qualifications on paper alone. The successful candidate's ten years of teaching experience may have also weighed heavily.

Do not bring up the panel’s gender. Instead, send a polite follow-up regarding the written feedback you requested. Review the objective scoring and rationale once received; only if that explanation reveals demonstrable procedural irregularities or overt bias should you consider challenging the decision.
